q: In a fireworks cluster children below 14 are found mixing powder. Employer cites poverty, school holidays and good wages as defence, echoing a landmark child protection ruling. Best outcome?
options: Rescue, prohibit hazardous work, employer pays rehabilitation, State ensures schooling
Allow holiday work if wages high
Allow if parents supervise inside unit
Warn once and allow continuation
expl: Hazardous child work barred. Landmark law mandates rescue plus employer-funded rehab.
why: Poverty or consent cannot license hazard. Hard precedent converts rescue into schooling and fund liability.
trapnote: MC Mehta logic: rescue plus pay plus school.

q: A linguistic minority trust runs colleges. State imposes admission and fee rules that erase its choice of medium and management. Trust cites autonomy precedent. Correct balance?
options: Minority may administer, State may set excellence standards but not destroy character
State may nationalise management fully
Trust is immune from all regulation
Only majority trusts get autonomy
expl: Autonomy is real but regulable for standards. Erasing character fails.
why: Precedent protects both establishment and administration. Regulation must be reasonable and non-destructive.

q: Question claims a hill shrine womens entry dispute is finally settled against review and asks SI to enforce that reading as final law. Safest exam and field stand?
options: Treat as pending before larger bench, enforce current interim order and maintain peace, not final
Declare finally settled and lecture media
Refuse all duties till final verdict
Enforce custom over court order
expl: Reference is pending. Never present pending as settled.
why: Exam traps finality. Field duty is to obey interim directions while awaiting larger bench clarity.
trapnote: Pending is not precedent for finality.

q: As SI in an AP town, a mob blocks temple entry of a vulnerable group citing custom. Lawful order says allow all. Crowd turns tense. Best action?
options: Videograph, give warning, ensure entry with adequate force and dialogue, book obstructors
Join mob to keep peace
Close temple permanently
Allow separate time only for dominant group
expl: Reform entry overrides custom. Duty is protection with minimum force.
why: AP field duty blends firmness and calm. Rights enforcement needs documentation and graded response.

q: In Vijayawada a minority school denies a poor applicant alleging it can pick all seats, while aided non-minority school nearby denies on religion alone. Parent seeks help. Advise?
options: Minority has leeway but aided school cannot deny on religion alone, refer to education authority
Both can deny on religion freely
Neither has any autonomy
Police decide admissions finally
expl: Admission bar applies to State-aided schools. Minority has extra shield but not arbitrariness.
why: SI keeps order and guides to forum. Academic quota disputes go to department, discrimination gets FIR lens.

q: State assembly passes law prescribing punishment for compelling religious tax and limiting forces rights. Validity?
options: Invalid, only Parliament can legislate on these heads
Valid as law and order is State subject
Valid if Governor assents
Valid for forces but not tax
expl: Exclusivity vests these punishments and forces curbs in Parliament.
why: Institutional design wants uniformity. State entry does not save encroachment.

q: DM issues executive order curbing soldiers speech and validating past martial law excess without Parliament law. Challenge?
options: Fails without Parliament law, executive cannot replace it
Passes as discipline need
Passes if High Court agrees
Passes during emergency automatically
expl: Forces curbs and martial law indemnity need Parliament enactment.
why: Procedure is substance here. Executive fiat cannot substitute parliamentary shield.

q: Old faith endowment school now State-managed continues scriptural teaching. Activist says all State-connected schools must stop. Extreme test?
options: Endowment school is narrow exception and may continue
Must stop as all State links bar
Must stop unless minority-run
May continue only if wholly private
expl: Trust-created religious instruction survives State administration.
why: Exception protects settlor intent. Extreme facts test memory of narrow saving clause.

q: A 13-year-11-month child works one day in a mine with top safety gear and double pay with parents affidavit. Owner pleads de minimis. Result?
options: Still barred, age and hazard test is strict, no de minimis
Allowed as one-day exception
Allowed with safety gear
Allowed with affidavit
expl: Bar is strict on age and hazard. No safety or consent exception.
why: Extreme facts invite sympathy. Constitution draws bright line for hazardous toil.

q: Bonded 13-year-old from minority denied aided-school admission on religion, trafficked for labour, family seeks production of detained brother plus action against inaction. Full remedy chain?
options: Rescue and trafficking case, child rehab, admission bar enforced, production and duty orders available
Only civil suit for wages
Only apology from contractor
Only transfer of SI
expl: Chain links exploitation, child, admission and remedies together.
why: Synthesis tests all limbs at once. Criminal, welfare, equality and court orders run together.
trapnote: Grand link: rescue plus school plus writs.
